sections.h2: Where is Red Willow County and what is in it?
sections.html:
Red Willow County lies along Nebraska's southern line, with its south boundary touching Kansas. It covers 718 square miles, nearly all of it land, and the Republican River runs east through the north-central part. The terrain is rolling hills that slope to the east, and the low ground in the river drainage is farmed.

The county was formed in 1873 and named for Red Willow Creek. According to its reference entry, the name is thought to be a mistranslation of the Dakota name Chanshasha Wakpala, which means Red Dogwood Creek. McCook is the county seat. The other incorporated places are the city of Indianola and the villages of Bartley, Danbury and Lebanon, and Marion, Perry and Shippee are unincorporated communities.

Part of the Red Willow Reservoir State Wildlife Management Area is inside the county, and the neighbors are Furnas, Hitchcock and Frontier counties in Nebraska plus Decatur and Rawlins counties in Kansas.

sections.h2: How many people live in Red Willow County?
sections.html:
Red Willow County had 10,702 residents in the 2020 census and an estimated 10,307 in 2025, a drop of 3.7 percent. The count has slipped at each census since 1980, when it was 12,615. The highest count on record is 13,859 in 1930, so the 2025 estimate is about 26 percent below the peak. In a county that has lost people for decades, some owners prefer a quick as-is sale to a long listing.

A vacancy rate of 12.1 percent is worth knowing if you own a house you do not live in. An empty house still gets a tax bill, and it ages faster without someone checking the roof, the furnace and the plumbing.

sections.h2: What is McCook like as a county seat?
sections.html:
McCook was platted in 1882 when the Burlington and Missouri River Railroad reached the site, and it was named for Union Army Brigadier General Alexander McDowell McCook. The city covers about 5.4 square miles.

It is also the home of the first two-year junior college in Nebraska, founded in September 1926 on the second floor of the YMCA building and now part of the Mid-Plains system. The McCook Economic Development Corporation works to keep and attract businesses in the area, and the George Norris House is on the National Register of Historic Places.

sections.h2: How do the weather and the Republican River affect a Red Willow County house?
sections.html:
McCook has a hot-summer humid continental climate with cold, dry winters and hot, humid summers. The annual precipitation normal is 22.53 inches, mostly from May through August, and snowfall averages 28.8 inches a season, mostly from November through April.

  • An average of 45 days a year reach 90 degrees Fahrenheit or higher, and 5.4 days reach 100.
  • About 28 days a year stay at or below freezing all day, and 8.6 days dip to 0 or lower.
  • Records run from minus 30 degrees on January 12, 1912 to 115 on June 26, 2012.

Swings that wide are hard on roofing, siding, exposed plumbing and older windows. Knowing your own list of deferred repairs before you decide how to sell avoids surprises later.

sections.h2: What roads, rail and schools connect Red Willow County?
sections.html:
McCook sits on U.S. Routes 6, 34 and 83, and Nebraska Highway 89 also crosses the county. U.S. 83 runs north to North Platte and Interstate 80, and U.S. 34 links west to Colorado and east toward Hastings and Lincoln.

Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at McCook station. Denver Air Connection runs commercial flights from McCook Regional Airport to Denver.

sections.h2: Who bills Red Willow County property tax, and how is it paid?
sections.html:
The Red Willow County Treasurer collects real estate tax from an office at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook. The mailing address is PO Box 490, McCook, NE 69001, and the phone is 308-345-6515, extension 1. Taxes can be looked up and paid online through the state's tax portal, for current and back taxes alike. A card payment carries a 2.35 percent convenience fee with a $2.00 minimum, and an e-check costs $2.00.

The county assessor, Lori Stevens, is at the same address and can be reached at 308-345-4388 or assessor@redwillowcountyne.gov, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays through lunch. The assessor sets values on all real and personal property, keeps the parcel maps and prepares the tax roll for the treasurer. The office also answers questions about homestead exemption eligibility.

sections.h2: What can change a Red Willow County valuation?
sections.html:
The assessor's page names four things that move a value: shifts in the market, outside influences on the property, adding or removing improvements, and a remodel or rehab. A new garage or a finished basement raises the number, and tearing down an old outbuilding should lower it.

If you disagree, the protest must reach the County Clerk on or before June 30 and must give the value you are asking for and the reasons. Under Statute 77-1502, the clerk mails the board's decision by August 2, and you then have until August 24 to appeal to the Tax Equalization and Review Commission under Statute 77-1510. Exemptions are available for educational and religious facilities and for qualifying seniors or people with disabilities.

sections.h2: What happens at the Red Willow County tax sale?
sections.html:
The county holds its tax sale on the first Monday in March, and the 2026 sale was March 2 in the courthouse. The delinquent list is advertised for three consecutive weeks in February in the local paper and online.

  • A buyer purchases the delinquent tax, not the property, and pays later years' taxes as they come due.
  • The redemption period is three years at 14 percent interest.
  • If the owner has not redeemed after three years, the certificate holder has six months to foreclose.
  • Registration costs $25 and the county charges $20 per certificate sold.

The treasurer's page says the office will not give legal advice to certificate buyers and points them to Nebraska statutes 77-1801 through 77-1941, so an attorney is the right call for your own parcel.

sections.h2: How does a Red Willow County sale close with tax owed?
sections.html:
The title company asks the treasurer for the payoff, collects it from the proceeds and records the deed. The seller also pays Nebraska's documentary stamp tax through the register of deeds, which the Department of Revenue sets at $3.32 for each $1,000 of value for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

If the taxes have already gone to the March sale, redeeming the certificate has to come first. Send us the parcel number and we can look at the numbers with you.

faqs.q: When do Red Willow County taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: The first half becomes delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1. The dates follow Nebraska Statute 77-204, so unpaid first-half tax is delinquent from May 1.

faqs.q: How do I protest my Red Willow County valuation?
faqs.a: Send your protest to the County Clerk on or before June 30, stating the value you are asking for and why. The county board of equalization hears it, and its decision can be appealed to the state commission.

faqs.q: Who is the Red Willow County Assessor?
faqs.a: Lori Stevens is the assessor, at 502 Norris Avenue in McCook, phone 308-345-4388. The office is open weekdays 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can I pay Red Willow County property tax by card?
faqs.a: Yes, online through the tax portal, with a 2.35 percent convenience fee and a $2.00 minimum. An e-check costs $2.00, and you can also mail a payment to PO Box 490, McCook.

faqs.q: What is the Red Willow County tax sale?
faqs.a: It is the annual sale of tax certificates for unpaid real estate tax, held the first Monday in March. Certificates carry 14 percent interest, and the county's page gives a three-year redemption period.

faqs.q: Does Red Willow County have a vacancy problem?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 5,157 housing units, with 12.1 percent vacant. Population fell to 10,702 in 2020 and to an estimated 10,307 in 2025.
